notes.title: Heroine Prologues Update + Issue With Old Saves
notes.content:
[h2]Heroine Prologues Update[/h2]
Hello everyone!

After a few hiccups, we are pleased to announced the release of our Heroine Prologues Update for Lucid9. In it, you will find:
[list]
[*]The addition of "Heroine Prologues", scenes that will act as the beginning story for each heroine's route, narrated from their own PIV. This content will appear on the start screen once the game has been completed the first time.
[*]A mysterious "UNDO" option which replaces the START button in the main menu (it will lead you to the prologues).
[*]Updated artwork for a number of returning characters as well as artwork for new characters joining the cast.
[*]Minor text and grammar issues have also been fixed.
[*]Between 1 and 2 hours of new content, a sneak-peek of what's to come!
[/list]

[h2]Issue With Old Saves[/h2]

Last week, we briefly pushed this update, only to find out people were having trouble loading their old saves, as it would pop up an error before returning them to the beginning of the game.

We found out this was due to Lucid9: Inciting Incident using an older version of our engine, Ren'py, than what we have been using to develop the rest of the game. This was an unexpected problem on our part, and we apologize. Sadly, we couldn't find an easy fix to this problem without undoing months of work in the game's code.

Which is why we eventually came up with an alternative solution: older saves made in Lucid9: Inciting Incident prior to this update will automatically go through a "compatibility fix". If you load one of these saves, [u][b]you won't be loaded in the exact spot as you were before, but rather the beginning of the Day / Chapter in which the save was made[/b][/u]. This will only happen [b]once[/b], after which you'll be able to save and load normally.

We apologize, as this will certainly be inconvenient for some our players, but we of Fallen Snow Studios ultimately decided this was the best solution to ensure development going forward is as smooth as possible. Again, we are sorry, and we promise this will not happen again.

Thank you for your patience and continuous support, and we hope you enjoy this new addition to the story!

notes.title: Lucid9 Heroine Prologues Release: December 15th!
notes.content:
After a long wait, the heroine prologues release is now finished and ready to be released on Steam this very December 15th!

As we previously described, the Heroine Prologues contain the first chapter for each of the four heroine routes in Lucid9, plus a little bit of additional content written solely for this release! Be advised that these chapters serve only as introductory pieces to the remainder of our game, narrated from the POV of each one of the heroines. Rest assured, however, that Yama will return as the overall protagonist and narrator in future releases.

We're extremely excited to finally share a portion of the content we'd been working on. It's certainly a milestone for us, and we hope that it sparks interest for the heroine routes that is still yet to come.

To give you some insight of what to expect from the prologues, here's a quick list:

- Dope, new music tracks.
- Bad writing from a prominent political figure. 
- (ง •̀_•́)ง ​
- Lemonade drink drunk by a lemonade boy. 
- Good Dads & Shady Moms. 
- A crotch rocket.

In order to access this new content, you need to first have reached the ending of Lucid9: Inciting Incident. Once you do, you will notice that the main menu theme has changed, along with something else. Simply find this new option to see what we have in store!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/23787815/125e611664afdbfaf4107f5a0faa0b14c40586a5.png[/img]

Additionally, some time after the 15th, we'll be streaming the prologues on our Twitch channel. Be sure to tune in if you're interested to learn more about its development.

We will post a new blog entry on the very same day, with new information about Lucid9’s future. Thank you for your patience, and we hope you enjoy!

- Fallen Snow Studios

notes.title: Inciting Incident Voice Acting Patch and Prologue Scenes
notes.content:
October has come around. For some, this marks the beginning of Fall, meaning fallen leaves, cold weather and Halloween. For others like myself, this is when the climate starts heating up… or it would if only global warming wasn’t a thing. But hey, at least Halloween is the same. Halloween might be a time for scares in a safe and healthy environment, but there’s nothing scary about this blog entry! Quite the opposite, in fact, given that we have a couple of exciting news to announce.

But first, let’s get the obligatory information out of the way. Progress is going smoothly, with writers, artists and composers all making steady progress since the last update. Those who joined the team recently have caught up successfully with everything that has been done before, and all that’s left now is to keep working and finish this tale once and for all.

And talking about ongoing progress, the mythical voice patch is progressing smoothly and nearing completion. Soon, you’ll be able to play Lucid9: Inciting Incident again with the added benefit of NOT paying attention to the words on screen and instead listening to the wonderful voices of our talented cast of actors! We don’t have a release date (yet), but we promise to give you one once we have nailed down the specifics of this patch. I hope all of you are looking forward to this as much as I am.

As you know, it’s very difficult to give our followers a sneak-peak at the script itself, since Lucid9 is a plot-heavy visual novel, and any piece of writing could count as a potential game-ruining spoiler. That said, we are happy to announce that this is no longer the case.

After much discussion, us writers have decided to start work on releasing what we like to call “Prologue Scenes” to the public!

We call them Prologue Scenes, but they are not prequels of any sort to what you read in Lucid9: Inciting Incident. Rather, these short scenes serve as a prelude to the heroine routes, narrated from the point-of-view of the girls themselves. These occur shortly before the beginning of their routes (and in some cases, even further away in the past). While each scene varies in length, altogether they will add between 1 and 1 ½ hours of content to Lucid9. You will get to learn more about the society in Isamu 3 years in the future, as well as what sort of lives some of our characters have led after the tragic events at the Isamu Imperial Boarding Academy.

Originally, these scenes would only be accessible during the transition between Inciting Incident and the chosen heroine routes. But until the routes are finished and completed, you’ll have the option to read their prologues individually and at your leisure (after completing Inciting Incident, of course).

This is exciting news for us, since we’ve been itching to showcase our writing to the public! No release date for this either, but we will provide one (along with the voice patch’s, hopefully) in the coming months.

On another note, Elphaze has been working on Yama's new artwork. Big thanks to her for sharing it with us to include in this update!

See you next time!
Via - Fallen Snow Studios

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/23787815/f54392e3af6611d799ddceef5f359644bddb0326.png[/img]

notes.title: What you should know regarding the release
notes.content:
We're all very excited and very anxious regarding the release: it's the result of two years worth of effort that we are finally presenting to the world. But we believe that you, readers, should be the only ones deciding whether our work is something that will stay as a memorable story or not. We've done pretty much all we could to ensure that Lucid9 would be of the best quality possible, and we don't have any regrets regarding that.

Whether you've followed our project for a while, or whether you've just stumbled upon it a while ago through one of our numerous announcements (by the way, big thanks to Sekai Project for helping us spreading the awareness about Lucid9), I believe it would probably be a good idea to summarize all the stuff you should know about the release. I'm most likely only going to repeat stuff that was already said, but I want to avoid people starting to read Inciting Incident with false expectations. And maybe you'll be able to appreciate our work even more by knowing our circumstances?

[h1]Things you should know about the game in general:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]This release is the first part of Lucid9's story[/b]. I guess you could consider that Lucid9 is somehow episodic. If you're more familiar with how VNs work, Inciting Incident can identify as a common route, though unlike most VNs, this common route has a self-contained story and is actually plot driven. The next release (which should be a patch to the current release) should continue directly onto the different heroine routes, though we're still a long way to go.
[*][b]Inciting Incident is free, and the entirety of Lucid9 will be free as well.[/b] Though I can't swear that I'm a hundred percent sure it'll stay that way. The chances remain very high still, it's just that if it happens that going commercial is the only way to lead Lucid9 to completion, we might consider it.
[*][b]The voice acting patch is scheduled for 2017[/b]. We've been repeating that everywhere, but just to make sure, recording the lines of the voice actors is a lengthy process, especially when considering that all the voice actors are doing it for free as well, we can't expect them to put the recording sessions as one of their priority, which is only natural. Currently, nearly all of the lines for the first in game day has been recorded. We'll make sure to share progress regularly with you about that.
[/list]

[h1]Things you should know about the team:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]The creation of Lucid9 so far has been achieved with a $0 budget.[/b] While we're not exactly bragging about it (maybe a little), it's more of a reminder so that you can set up your expectations more accurately, and understand better our limitations. Basically, we have to work with what we have, and the people who agreed to offer their skills for our project. Beggars can't be choosers after all. Though I'm not one bit dissatisfied with how the end result turned out, and tons of people with amazing skills joined us in order to create a memorable and enjoyable game.
[*][b]We are all hobbyists working on Lucid9 in our free time.[/b] Which ties in directly with the previous point: for such a large scale game, we had to compensate our lack of available time involvement by more manpower. Which in turns can cause some slight issues, mainly some inconsistencies. Inconsistencies in art (male and female sprites), music, writing (though that won't be the case for Inciting Incident, since there was only one writer for 95% of the writing). Some people will argue that we could just have made a less ambitious game, shorter, with less characters, so that it could have required less assets. But to be honest, that's not what we wanted to do. And I believe that precisely because we were ambitious that we managed to interest and gather so many skilled people around us (though there's also luck factoring in the equation).
[/list]

[h1]Things you should know about the story: [/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Inciting Incident will be mostly linear.[/b] Still, the choices that you'll make can lead you to a bad ending. Those bad endings are quite interesting, and we'd recommend you to try reading one or two.
[*][b]You'll have lot of in game choices[/b], but since we didn't want to make the process too tedious for the reader, most of the mystery related sections are forgiving and the choices are set up in a way so that you never get stuck (except for two special instances that we'll let you discover yourself). Some of the choices are more important, as stated previously there are some moments where making a bad decision (or a series of bad decisions) will lead you to  a bad end.
[*][b]You'll be able to unlock in-game achievements[/b]: we hope that it will give some replay value to the game, though we made sure that the achievements wouldn't be too tedious and wouldn't require 10 different playthroughs to complete. We're not really fans of completion achievements, so you'll nearly only find choice related achievements, which ties in with the choice system we opted for in the mystery segments: you'll be rewarded with achievements if you don't end up picking the wrong choices during the investigations (and here is an additional challenge from us, try to earn those achievements on your first playthrough!)
[*][b]It has a Japanese setting.[/b] And we know that it will probably annoy a lot of people, and even probably instantly repulse some others. "Why not go for something more original?" some people often ask. Well, mostly because at the time, we wanted to make something that takes place in (fictional) Japan. And at the time (though it's still true now), what mattered wasn't what our possible audience would want to read, but what we wanted to do. And the more we progressed with our story conception, the more bothersome and difficult it became to change the setting, so naturally we never really questioned it. I won't deny that us being influenced by Japanese VNs played a big role in deciding the setting. But in the end, a setting is only a setting. At the end of the day, it's only a location, a language, a currency, and maybe a slightly different social system. Lucid9 could have happened pretty much anywhere without many big differences, though if I was given the chance to remake this choice, I'd probably think twice. But if some people want to judge our work and dismiss it solely based on the setting and without actually trying out the actual content, it'll be their loss I guess, they will just forbid themselves to experience our story because of their narrow-mindedness.
[/list]

[img]http://lucid9.weebly.com/uploads/2/0/3/1/20314597/384990_orig.jpg[/img]

A big thanks to the members of Fallen Snow Studios who worked very hard to make Lucid9 become a reality, and a big thanks to all the people who supported us up until now. We hope you'll enjoy reading Inciting Incident as much as we enjoyed creating it!
